RQ1.2: Is there a relationship between GPU usage and energy consumption when training DL models?

Santiago del Rey

Load data

df <- read_parquet("data/metrics/processed/clean-dl-training-energy-consumption-dataset.gzip") %>%
    rename(
        training_environment = `training environment`,
        gpu_usage = `gpu usage (%)`,
        energy = `energy (MJ)`,
        power_draw = `average gpu power (W)`,
        tdp = `max power limit (W)`,
    ) %>%
    filter(architecture != "inception_v3" & training_environment != "Desktop Normal User") %>%
    mutate(
        energy_per_image = (energy * 1000000) / `total seen images`, # Convert MJ to J and normalize by total seen images
        gpu_usage = gpu_usage / 100, # Convert percentage to proportion
        architecture = case_match(
            architecture,
            "mobilenet_v2" ~ "Mobilenet V2",
            "nasnet_mobile" ~ "NASNet Mobile",
            "resnet50" ~ "ResNet50",
            "xception" ~ "Xception",
            "vgg16" ~ "VGG16"
        ),
        architecture = factor(architecture, levels = c("Mobilenet V2", "NASNet Mobile", "ResNet50", "Xception", "VGG16")),
        training_environment = factor(training_environment, levels = c("Desktop ML Engineer", "Server")),
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(run_id, training_environment, architecture, gpu_usage, energy_per_image, power_draw, tdp)

filter_outliers <- function(df, variable) {
    df %>%
        group_by(architecture, training_environment) %>%
        mutate(
            Q1 = quantile(!!sym(variable), 0.25),
            Q3 = quantile(!!sym(variable), 0.75),
            IQR = Q3 - Q1,
            is_outlier = !!sym(variable) < (Q1 - 1.5 * IQR) | !!sym(variable) > (Q3 + 1.5 * IQR)
        ) %>%
        ungroup() %>%
        filter(!is_outlier) %>%
        dplyr::select(-Q1, -Q3, -IQR, -is_outlier)
}

# Detect outliers independently for each variable and keep the runs that are not outliers in any of them
keep_non_outliers <- function(df, variables) {
    kept <- df
    for (variable in variables) {
        kept <- semi_join(kept, filter_outliers(df, variable), by = "run_id")
    }
    kept
}

# Centre GPU usage so that the factor main effects are evaluated at the average GPU usage instead of at 0%
df_clean_energy <- keep_non_outliers(df, c("gpu_usage", "energy_per_image")) %>%
    mutate(gpu_usage_c = gpu_usage - mean(gpu_usage))

df_clean_power <- keep_non_outliers(df, c("gpu_usage", "power_draw")) %>%
    mutate(gpu_usage_c = gpu_usage - mean(gpu_usage))

# Set sum-to-zero contrasts in each model call so that Type III tests do not depend on global options
sum_contrasts <- list(architecture = "contr.sum", training_environment = "contr.sum")

Plot GPU usage vs energy consumption

gpu_vs_energy <- ggplot(df_clean_energy,
    aes(x = gpu_usage, y = energy_per_image, color = training_environment),
    size = 3, alpha = 0.7
) +
    geom_point() +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
    labs(
        x = "GPU Usage (%)",
        y = "Normalized Energy (J/image)",
    ) +
    guides(
        color = guide_legend(title = element_blank())
    )

gpu_vs_energy
## `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'

ggsave(
    plot = gpu_vs_energy + pub_theme,
    filename = file.path(fig_dir, "gpu_usage_vs_energy_consumption.pdf"),
    device = cairo_pdf,
    units = "cm",
    width = 10, height = 8, dpi = 300
)
## `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'

Plot GPU usage vs average power draw

server_tdp <- df_clean_power %>%
    filter(training_environment == "Server") %>%
    summarise(tdp = mean(tdp, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    pull(tdp)

desktop_tdp <- df_clean_power %>%
    filter(training_environment == "Desktop ML Engineer") %>%
    summarise(tdp = mean(tdp, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    pull(tdp)

gpu_vs_power <- ggplot(
    df_clean_power,
    aes(x = gpu_usage, y = power_draw, color = training_environment),
    size = 3, alpha = 0.7
) +
    geom_point() +
    geom_line(aes(y = gpu_usage * tdp, linetype = "dashed")) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, aes(linetype = "solid")) +
    # Add an element indicating that dashed lines represent TDP * GPU usage
    scale_linetype_manual(
        name = element_blank(),
        values = c("dashed", "solid"),
        labels = c("TDP x GPU usage", "Fit")
    ) +
    labs(
        x = "GPU Usage (%)",
        y = "Average Power Draw (W)",
    ) +
    guides(
        color = guide_legend(title = element_blank(), order = 1),
        linetype = guide_legend(order = 2)
    ) +
    theme(legend.direction = "vertical")


gpu_vs_power
## `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'

ggsave(
    plot = gpu_vs_power + pub_theme,
    filename = file.path(fig_dir, "gpu_usage_vs_power_draw.pdf"),
    device = cairo_pdf,
    units = "cm",
    width = 10, height = 8, dpi = 300
)
## `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'
gpu_vs_energy <- gpu_vs_energy +
    guides(color = "none")

gpu_usage_vs_power_and_energy <- (gpu_vs_energy | gpu_vs_power) +
    plot_layout(axes = "collect", guides = "collect")

ggsave(
    plot = gpu_usage_vs_power_and_energy & pub_theme,
    filename = file.path(fig_dir, "gpu_usage_vs_power_draw_and_energy.pdf"),
    device = cairo_pdf,
    units = "cm",
    width = 13.71, height = 9, dpi = 300
)
## `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'

Statistical analysis

Energy consumption analysis

Global linear trend

model_global <- lm(energy_per_image ~ gpu_usage, data = df_clean_energy)
summary(model_global)
## 
## Call:
## lm(formula = energy_per_image ~ gpu_usage, data = df_clean_energy)
## 
## Residuals:
##       Min        1Q    Median        3Q       Max 
## -0.154386 -0.084052 -0.009657  0.100395  0.149042 
## 
## Coefficients:
##             Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)    
## (Intercept)  0.09910    0.01807   5.483 9.61e-08 ***
## gpu_usage    0.21847    0.02406   9.079  < 2e-16 ***
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## Residual standard error: 0.0924 on 270 degrees of freedom
## Multiple R-squared:  0.2339, Adjusted R-squared:  0.2311 
## F-statistic: 82.43 on 1 and 270 DF,  p-value: < 2.2e-16
anova(model_global)
Model diagnostics
# Check residuals
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(model_global)

# Check residuals with DHARMa
sim_linear <- simulateResiduals(model_global)
testResiduals(sim_linear)

check_model(model_global)

Interaction effects

# Perform linear regression with centred GPU usage and sum-to-zero contrasts
model_linear <- lm(
    energy_per_image ~ gpu_usage_c * training_environment * architecture,
    data = df_clean_energy, contrasts = sum_contrasts
)
summary(model_linear)

# Type III ANOVA, classical and robust to unequal variances
anova_linear <- Anova(model_linear, type = 3)
anova_linear
Anova(model_linear, type = 3, white.adjust = "hc3")
## Coefficient covariances computed by hccm()
eta_squared(anova_linear, partial = FALSE, verbose = FALSE) # Eta² (total variance explained)
eta_squared(anova_linear, partial = TRUE, verbose = FALSE) # Partial Eta² (variance explained after controlling for others)

Because GPU usage interacts with both factors, we report its slope (J/image per unit of GPU usage) in each architecture and environment.

gpu_slopes <- emtrends(model_linear, ~ training_environment * architecture, var = "gpu_usage_c")
summary(gpu_slopes, infer = TRUE)

Mixed effects model

model_mixed <- lmer(energy_per_image ~ gpu_usage + (1 | architecture) + (1 | training_environment), data = df_clean_energy)
summary(model_mixed)

Post-hoc tests

# Estimate marginal means with GPU usage at 90% (0.9), expressed on the centred scale
emms <- emmeans(
    model_linear, ~ gpu_usage_c * training_environment * architecture,
    at = list(gpu_usage_c = 0.9 - mean(df_clean_energy$gpu_usage))
)
emms

## NOTE: If two or more means share the same grouping symbol,

ggplot(compact_letter_display, aes(
    x = interaction(training_environment, architecture),
    y = emmean
)) +
    geom_col(fill = "skyblue") +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL), width = 0.2) +
    geom_text(aes(label = .group), vjust = -0.5, color = "red") +
    labs(x = "Condition", y = "Estimated Marginal Mean (J/image) at 90% GPU Usage") +
    theme_pubr() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

Global linear trend

summary(model_global_power_draw)
